paper.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of a Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) Be low-density steels
paper.paper_scope: Systematically studies the effect of beryllium addition (0–1.5 wt%) on the density, microstructure (austenite/ferrite/Be–Fe phases/carbides) and mechanical properties of as-cast and hot-rolled Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C low-density steels.

alloys.description: Base low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C steel of the experimental series, without any beryllium addition. Used as the reference material against which the effect of Be is assessed.
alloys.alloys_notes: Made from high-purity elements Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%), C (99.99%).

processes.description: As-cast terminal state: alloy ingots prepared by vacuum induction melting under high-purity argon, diameter 60 mm and thickness 30 mm, with no heat treatment or thermal deformation applied.
processes.processes_notes: Shared terminal state applying to all four alloys (0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be); alloy_id left null because the state is not alloy-specific.

source.reason: Section 3.1 is dedicated to 'Microstructure and mechanical properties of as-cast states'; b0015 describes the vacuum induction melting of the ingots from which the as-cast state is obtained before any deformation.

processes.description: Hot-rolled terminal state: 17-pass hot rolling at 1050°C to a 5 mm plate (equivalent to 83% total deformation, 1.5 mm per pass, strain rate 0.6 s^-1), with 3 min reheating in a muffle furnace after each pass, followed by water cooling to room temperature after the final pass.
processes.processes_notes: Shares the prior as-cast ingot as its precursor (proc_as-cast); applied identically to all four alloys, so alloy_id is left null.

unmapped_findings: Density measured by Archimedes method for rolled steels: 0Be 6.54, 0.5Be 6.47, 1.0Be 6.36, 1.5Be 6.29 g/cm3; the 1.5Be density (≈6.29) is ~19.87% lower than a common steel grade (7.82 g/cm3) and 3.8% lower than the base Fe–Mn–Al–C steel (6.50 g/cm3).

DSC determined the phase transformation temperature of the Be-free steel as 1278.8 °C; Be addition lowered the transformation point by ~120 °C, with further slight decreases of ~1 °C (1.0Be) and 5 °C (1.5Be).

Microstructure transitions from single austenite (0Be, 0.5Be) to austenite + ferrite dual-phase (1.0Be, 1.5Be) with increasing Be; Be–Fe phases identified include Be11Fe, Be12Fe, Be2Fe and Be2C, plus AlFe3 and κ-carbides in 0Be.
